rationale: Point-in-time recovery only covers the last 35 days and stops protecting the data as soon as it is turned off, whereas on-demand backups are retained until explicitly deleted and survive the deletion of the table itself. A table with no on-demand backup therefore has no recovery option beyond the point-in-time recovery window, which is insufficient for data subject to longer retention requirements or for recovering from a corruption discovered late.
remediation: Create on-demand backups of the table, or place it under an AWS Backup plan with a retention period matching the data retention requirements
